newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money rates fall amid tax payments.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money rates fall amid tax payments.

text.p: Jakarta call money fell to 11.0 percent on Tuesday from 14.5 percent in the morning on the back of sufficient liquidity in the money market, dealers said.
They said weekly tax payments due Tuesday were lower than initially feared, allowing short-term rates to ease.
The central bank supplied 107 billion rupiah on Tuesday.
One-week money was last given at 11.75 percent. One- and three-month money were last given at 12.5 and 13.375 percent, respectively.
Dealers said the market was also well prepared to face the weekly tax payments as liquidity was boosted last week by an increase in one-week money.
The central bank has not announced the bilateral rates.
The bank offered one-week bilateral SBIs at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.25, one-month at 10.25, three-month at 10.75, six-month at 11.5 and one-year at 12.0 percent on Monday.
The average overnight interbank rate on Monday was 10.02 percent, compared with 10.19 percent on Friday.
